title: A Table Is Worth 64 Tokens: Pixel-level Compression for Multi-Table Document Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2608.26949v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Answering questions over real-world documents requires processing long inputs that interleave text with tables. Optical context compression, which represents context as images, promises to reduce token cost, but its effect on table understanding remains unclear. We study pixel-level table compression for question answering over documents with multiple tables, evaluating five VLMs across two benchmarks and five visual-token budgets. Representing tables as images at native resolution matches text in both performance and efficiency, but downscaling them makes models compensate the loss in readability with longer, less effective reasoning traces that cancel the expected savings. Highly downscaled tables, however, preserve enough signal to identify whether they are relevant to a question. translated_title: 一表抵64词元：多表格文档问答中的像素级压缩
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26949v1 公告类型：新 摘要：回答现实世界文档中的问题需要处理长输入，其中文本与表格交错。光学上下文压缩将上下文表示为图像，有望降低词元成本，但其对表格理解的影响仍不清楚。我们研究了多表格文档问答中的像素级表格压缩，在两个基准和五种视觉词元预算下评估了五种视觉语言模型。以原生分辨率将表格表示为图像，在性能和效率上与文本相当，但缩小它们会使模型用更长、效果较差的推理轨迹来补偿可读性的损失，从而抵消预期的节省。然而，高度缩小的表格保留了足够的信号来识别它们是否与问题相关。我们利用这种不对称性，提出一种无需训练的两步方法：模型首先从像素压缩的上下文中识别回答问题所需的表格。
tldr: 本文发现像素级表格压缩在原生分辨率下性能与文本相当，但高度缩小后仍可识别表格相关性，据此提出无需训练的两步法以提高多表格文档问答效率。
en_tdlr: This paper finds pixel-level table compression matches text performance at native resolution, yet highly downscaled tables retain relevance signals, leading to a training-free two-step method for efficient multi-table document QA.
